links.outcome: Error-detection yield of human review by flag tier and random sample of unflagged records
links.effect: HITL reviewed 289 records: cosine-flagged 62.4% had errors, RAG-fallback 78.6%, random nonflagged 3.8%; accuracy rose 86.0% to 97.0% after HITL.
links.quote: Among these, 93 records were flagged by cosine similarity (58 contained at least one extraction error, 62.4%), 14 by the RAG fallback mechanism (11 contained errors, 78.6%), and 182 were randomly sampled nonflagged records (7 contained errors, 3.8%).

links.outcome: Extraction accuracy before and after RAG-based verification against source text
links.effect: Accuracy increased from 74.8% (rule-based) to 86.0% after RAG validation; grounding accuracy 91.5%; improvement significant (P<0.001).
links.quote: After RAG-based contextual validation, accuracy increased further to 86.0% (95% CI, 83.6% to 88.4%), with F1 score and variable-level F1 both 0.813 (95% CI, 0.791 to 0.835).

links.outcome: Accuracy gains from automated rule-based and similarity-based checks on LLM outputs
links.effect: Rule-based verification raised accuracy from 64.9% to 74.8%; fully automated pipeline reached 86.0% (all P<0.001).
links.quote: With the addition of rule-based verification, performance improved to an accuracy of 74.8% (95% CI, 72.1% to 77.5%), F1 score of 0.701 (95% CI, 0.670 to 0.732), and variable-level F1 of 0.662 (95% CI, 0.631 to 0.693).

links.outcome: Extraction accuracy after clinician review of AI-extracted data
links.effect: Accuracy improved from 86.0% after automated validation to 97.0% (95% CI, 95.7% to 98.3%) following human-in-the-loop review.
links.quote: The final HITL review achieved the highest data fidelity, yielding an accuracy of 97.0% (95% CI, 95.7% to 98.3%), F1 score of 0.920 (95% CI, 0.879 to 0.961), and variable-level F1 of 0.902 (95% CI, 0.841 to 0.962), with grounding accuracy increasing to 93.2% (95% CI, 91.7% to 94.7%).

links.outcome: Awareness of dataset shift/generalizability limits of single-site pipeline
links.effect: Authors state no external validation; 0.82 similarity threshold would need recalibration; cited external accuracy reductions exceeding 20% for single-institution NLP models.
links.quote: The 0.82 similarity threshold, derived empirically from our institutional corpus, would require recalibration in new deployment settings.

links.outcome: Performance of English-pretrained SLM on Korean clinical text
links.effect: Korean token-to-character ratio 1.14 vs English 0.4-0.6 suggests suboptimal tokenization; acceptable performance reported after fine-tuning, but no language-stratified performance comparison.
links.quote: The application of an English-pretrained SLM to Korean-language text introduces linguistic challenges.

links.outcome: Absence of prospective/shadow-mode validation before clinical integration
links.effect: Retrospective single-center study; authors recommend shadow mode deployment and prospective accuracy audit before prospective clinical integration.
links.quote: Prior to prospective clinical integration, a staged validation process—including shadow mode deployment, prospective accuracy audit, and formal clinical impact assessment—is recommended to ensure patient safety and regulatory compliance.

links.effect: Errors occurred in 62.4% cosine-flagged, 78.6% RAG-fallback, and 3.8% random nonflagged records.

links.outcome: Stroke outcome model discrimination
links.effect: TabPFN AUROC 0.816 vs CatBoost 0.789 and logistic regression 0.700.
